profile.campus: LightEdge Des Moines campus, Altoona, IA (DC1 and DC2, adjacent buildings on Northridge Circle)
profile.reading:
LightEdge Des Moines 2, also called DC2, sits at 1401 Northridge Circle in Altoona, Iowa, immediately next to LightEdge's other Des Moines-area building on the same street. Per LightEdge's own combined specification sheet for the two-building site, the pair together provide 6.1 megawatts of critical IT load and 10.6 megawatts of total generator capacity with N+1 UPS redundancy, across 78,000 total square feet including 40,000 square feet of technical white space. LightEdge's sheet does not break those totals down between DC1 and DC2 individually, so no single-building capacity or square-footage figure is assigned to this specific record, and the same combined figures are recorded on the DC1 entry in this registry rather than duplicated as if each building carried the full campus total on its own.

A 2024 LightEdge leadership-transition announcement credits the company with building the first greenfield colocation data center in Iowa, though the release does not name or date a specific building among the Des Moines site's facilities, so that claim is presented here as company-level context rather than attributed to DC2 specifically. The facility carries a broad, compliance-oriented certification set common across LightEdge's portfolio, including SOC 1, 2, and 3, ISO 27001, 20000-1, and 22301, HITRUST, HIPAA and HITECH readiness, and PCI DSS, alongside NIST 800-53 and 800-171 alignment, with ten on-net carriers including Verizon, Lumen, Windstream, and Zayo.

LightEdge Solutions was founded in 1996 and is headquartered in Des Moines, Iowa. The company announced a new partnership with GI Partners, a private equity and real estate investment firm that also helped create Digital Realty in 2004, in September 2021. Then-CEO Jim Masterson said at the time that the deal would not change management, operations, or customer teams. Masterson led the company for 21 years before moving to an advisory board role at the end of 2024, and Rob Carter succeeded him as CEO on January 1, 2025. LightEdge describes its current footprint as 20 data centers across 12 US metro markets, including Kansas City, Omaha, Ashburn, Phoenix, San Jose, and St. Louis alongside Des Moines, Austin, San Diego, and Minneapolis, plus one location in Amsterdam, Netherlands. No tenant is named publicly for this specific building.

Altoona sits just east of downtown Des Moines and has grown into a suburban technology and light-industrial corridor. The same suburb is also home to one of Meta's flagship data center campuses, which Facebook first opened in 2014 after choosing the area partly for access to wind-generated power from MidAmerican Energy, though Meta's much larger campus is a separate operation with no ownership or operational connection to LightEdge's smaller enterprise colocation site on Northridge Circle. LightEdge's decision to concentrate its own Iowa infrastructure in Altoona rather than in the Des Moines city core reflects the same land and power-availability considerations that shape data center site selection nationally.

reading.body:
LightEdge Des Moines 2 sits in Altoona, Iowa as one building in a two-building campus that together publish 6.1 megawatts of critical IT load across 40,000 square feet of technical white space. The operator does not break this combined figure between DC1 and DC2, so the capacity attributable to this specific building is not published. At typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, the campus's 6.1 megawatts of IT load corresponds roughly to 150 racks, though this is an assumption about workload mix and not an operator claim.

The facility qualifies to host HIPAA and HITECH workloads, PCI DSS applications, NIST 800-53 and 800-171 aligned operations, and general enterprise compliance under SOC 1, 2, and 3 and ISO certifications. Ten on-net carriers including Verizon and Lumen provide transit. The campus sits in Altoona partly because the suburb offers power availability and land economics favorable to data center siting, factors that also attracted Meta's separate and much larger campus to the same area in 2014.

This campus ranks third by published megawatts in Iowa, behind two larger facilities. Only two of Iowa's 52 mapped data center sites publish power capacity figures. The state's total published capacity is 18 megawatts, making LightEdge Des Moines 2's share one-third of the state's disclosed infrastructure. Iowa publishes less capacity data than most US states with meaningful data center footprints.
